question:
A 36-year-old male seeks medical attention for a persistent headache following a car accident where
his forehead impacted the windshield. He describes an occipital headache with pressure sensation
behind his eyes. He reports no loss of consciousness, vomiting, or visual changes post-accident, and
has no significant medical history. Physical assessment shows: * Normal neurological findings *
Forehead contusion without open wounds or bleeding * Limited flexion and extension of the
sphenobasilar synchondrosis (SBS) during vault hold * Diminished rate and amplitude of the cranial
rhythmic impulse (CRI) What is the most appropriate therapeutic intervention for this case? Answer
Choices: (A) Balanced ligamentous tension of the SBS (B) Cranial lift technique (C) Indirect technique
for the temporal bones (D) Counterstrain of the occipital muscles (E) V spread (F) Suboccipital release
(G) Decompression of the occipital condyles (H) Compression of the fourth ventricle (I) High-velocity,
low-amplitude (HVLA) technique at the SBS (J) Direct myofascial release of the occipital region

A. High-velocity, low-amplitude (HVLA) technique at the SBS
B. Direct myofascial release of the occipital region
C. Indirect technique for the temporal bones
D. Decompression of the occipital condyles
E. Cranial lift technique
F. Balanced ligamentous tension of the SBS
G. Compression of the fourth ventricle
H. V spread
I. Counterstrain of the occipital muscles
J. Suboccipital release
